chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:

I read in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) wrote a treaty between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and those who joined them from the people of Yathrib: That every raiding party that raids with us, one supports the other with fairness and equity among the Muslims; and that no sanctuary is granted except with the permission of its people; and that the neighbor is like the self, neither harming nor sinning; and the sanctity of the neighbor is like the sanctity of his mother and father; a Muslim does not make peace alone without other Muslims in a battle in the cause of Allah, except on the basis of justice and equality.'

key_terms.الْجَارَ كَالنَّفْسِ: The neighbor is like the self
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالْأَنْصَارِ: The Muhajirun and the Ansar (Emigrants and Helpers)

ai.seo_question: What are the key legal provisions regarding neighbors and peace treaties in the Treaty of Ali?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the Prophetic treaty’s emphasis on collective military responsibility and the sanctity of neighborhood rights, reflecting the early Islamic legal framework for social cohesion. It underscores the principle that a believer cannot make peace independently without the consensus of the community, ensuring justice and equality in conflict resolution. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the interplay between individual rights and communal obligations in Shia jurisprudence.
